risk_assessment.rationale: The alert meets Rule 106001 and carries a high‑severity indicator, with 47 matching evidence items; however, because neither the source IP nor any involved domains have known reputation data, confidence is medium.

recommended_actions: Escalate to a human analyst for manual review
recommended_actions_freeform_experimenta: Initiate an immediate internal phishing awareness drill targeting the victimcorp domain to reinforce safe‑email practices, especially around audit‑related requests.

Deploy a temporary block or quarantine rule for any outbound mail from jane.tan@meridian-audit.com until further verification can be performed; this will prevent potential credential harvesting if the account is compromised.

Conduct a forensic review of the Mimecast logs to identify any other messages that may have been routed through the same IP (209.85.220.41) or domain patterns, and cross‑reference with internal user activity for anomalies.

Engage the vendor’s threat intelligence team to request deeper analysis on the 47 evidence items flagged by the correlation engine—particularly looking for any known malicious attachments or embedded URLs that may have been missed in the initial scan.

If possible, perform a reverse‑lookup of the IP address and domain names using external reputation services (e.g., AbuseIPDB, VirusTotal) to gather additional context; even if no provider data is available, community reports can surface hidden malicious activity.

Set up an automated alert that notifies the security operations center whenever any email from meridian‑audit.com or victimcorp.com contains suspicious keywords such as “Audit evidence request” or “Q2 access reviews,” ensuring rapid triage for future incidents.
triage_rationale_experimental: The alert shows high severity and a large number of correlated evidence items, yet the lack of known IP/domain reputation data and absence of definitive malicious payloads leave enough ambiguity to warrant further investigation before labeling it a true or false positive.
